bugs.error_message: P12 cutout pin diverged: Rust Simplex.cutout_from_simplex produced 7 pieces vs oracle 5 (corners 1/2 got 2 zero-length division lines instead of 1)
root_cause: Simplex.calcDivisionLines mixes TWO Java Direction-comparison flavors, and the port initially conflated them. (1) The NULL guards use reference equality: currentProjectionDir == Direction.NULL is true only for the shared constant that Point.perpendicularDirection returns in its collinear branch; translating that as == on IntDirection failed because IntDirection PartialEq mirrors Java .equals (collinear side + positive projection) under which distinct NULL instances are UNEQUAL — so the zero direction never matched and the guards never fired (the original 7-vs-5 piece divergence). (2) The final comparison Simplex.java:1137 is firstProjectionDir.equals(secondProjectionDir) — VALUE equality, NOT reference ==; an interim fix translated it as an object-identity flag, which was a misreading (caught in the Task 7 spec review): an identity flag diverges from .equals whenever the two directions are value-equal but distinct objects, which is reachable with raw parallel same-direction outer line pairs.
fix: NULL guards now use IntDirection::is_null() (zero-vector check; sound because the shared constant is the only zero direction those call sites can produce). The final comparison is plain Rust first_projection_dir == second_projection_dir, which IS Java .equals (T9 contract). Oracle pin PB9 (raw outer simplex with a duplicated same-direction bottom line, sharp inner triangle corner (4,0)) drives the second-division scan through the value-equal twin and pins the 2-division-line outcome.

bugs.root_cause: The resolver clamps/mirrors the settings' per-layer cost rows against the BOARD's layer count; an empty settings matrix is a caller-contract violation (every real settings source materializes one row per layer), and the clamp path silently produced the impossible zero-layer table instead of failing at the seam.
bugs.fix: Caller contract asserted: resolve_trace_costs is only called with a per-layer matrix (BatchSettings::new builds it from the IR; the probe's settings witness shows Java's RouterSettings(board) always fills one row per layer via applyBoardSpecificOptimizations). Lesson: clamp-into-empty hides the caller bug one frame downstream — fail at the seam, not the consumer.

bugs.task: M3-T12: Polyline::new vs Polyline::from_two_corners in test worlds
bugs.error_message: Anchor-trace inserts built with Polyline::new produced traces whose corner reads (first_corner/last_corner in the net-94 dump rows) came out wrong/empty.
bugs.root_cause: Polyline::new takes the full corner arrangement (with the closed-array semantics); two-corner open segments must go through from_two_corners, which sets the open-polyline bookkeeping the corner accessors read. The wrong ctor still produced a 'valid' object, so the error surfaced only in the row geometry.
bugs.fix: All test-world trace inserts use Polyline::from_two_corners (matches the Rust insert path's expectations; the jar's own two-point inserts carry exactly one segment).

bugs.task: M3-T13: corner_to_int written against a Point::Float variant that does not exist
bugs.error_message: corner_to_int (io.specctra.scope.Wiring rounding view) was first drafted as a three-arm match on Point::Int | Point::Float | Point::Rational; rustc rejected Point::Float — the enum is exactly Int(IntPoint) | Rational(Box<RationalPoint>).
bugs.root_cause: Mental-model drift from the Java side: Java Point has an int subclass and the wiring code touches coordinates as doubles freely; the Rust port collapsed the float face into RationalPoint::to_float() -> FloatPoint (fields pub(crate), so external crates must go through to_float). bugs.task: M3-T13 fix round: router_introduced_count floored at i32::MIN, not 0

Readers were already safe (atomic rename); only writer-writer interleaving was exposed. Lesson: an atomic-rename publish pattern is not writer-safe — tmp+rename needs its own exclusion whenever more than one thread can write.
